# Test PKI

**Test only. The private keys are unprotected and public.**

Generated by `scripts/gen-testpki.sh testdata/pki` on 2026-10-08 with
OpenSSL 3.0.13 (30 Jan 2024). Validity: 10 years (until 2036-10-05), so the
committed files don't expire during development.

| Files | What |
|---|---|
| `bp{256,384,512}-ca` | self-signed Brainpool CAs (brainpoolP256r1/P384r1/P512r1; ecdsa-with-SHA256/384/512) |
| `bp{256,384,512}-server`, `-client` | end entities on the CA's curve (serverAuth with `localhost`/`127.0.0.1`, clientAuth) |
| `bp256-evil-ca` | same subject as `bp256-ca`, another key (negative test N2) |
| `bp256-wrongkey` | a key only: a server that signs with it instead of `bp256-server.key` (negative test N1) |
| `rsa-ca`, `rsa-server`, `rsa-client` | RSA 2048 identities, for dual-identity tests (A_22453) |
| `p256-ca`, `bp256-under-p256`, `p256-under-bp256` | mixed chains: a Brainpool leaf under a P-256 CA, and the reverse |

File types:

- `*.pem`: certificate;
- `*.key`: private key, PKCS #8 (`BEGIN PRIVATE KEY`);
- `*.sec1.pem`: the EC keys again in SEC 1 (`BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY`, named
  curve).

Checks on 2026-10-08: every chain verifies with `openssl verify`; the evil
CA is rejected; OpenSSL ↔ OpenSSL mutual TLS 1.2 with the bp256 files
negotiated ECDHE brainpoolP256r1 with ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384.

Regenerating changes every key and certificate; tests must not depend on
specific values.
